item.text: I found the key semantic gap: the old schema made `request_id` globally unique even when an `idempotencyKey` was supplied, so a reused trace ID could incorrectly reject a separate payment. I’ve added a startup migration to remove that uniqueness constraint while preserving request-ID lookup, plus a regression test for two keyed payments sharing a trace ID.

item.text: One important concurrency detail surfaced during review: removing `request_id` uniqueness outright would weaken the legacy no-key guarantee under simultaneous retries. I’m tightening the migration to use a conditional unique key—unique only when no idempotency key is present—so both legacy and keyed semantics remain safe across instances.
